title: CKD definition and GFR categories
text: CKD is defined by abnormalities of kidney structure or function present for more than 3 months. GFR categories (mL/min/1.73m2): G1 90 or above, G2 60-89, G3a 45-59, G3b 30-44, G4 15-29, G5 below 15. Albuminuria categories A1-A3 add prognostic information. title: Metformin and kidney function
text: Metformin labeling: contraindicated when eGFR is below 30. Starting metformin is not recommended when eGFR is 30-45. If eGFR falls below 45 in a patient already taking it, the benefit and risk of continuing should be assessed; dose reduction is commonly considered. title: SGLT2 inhibitors and early eGFR change
text: SGLT2 inhibitors commonly cause a small, early, usually reversible fall in eGFR after initiation (a hemodynamic effect). This alone is generally not a reason to stop, but renal function should be rechecked. (Illustrative paraphrase for a demo, not clinical guidance; verify against the original guideline or label.)

title: HbA1c thresholds and targets
text: HbA1c of 6.5% or above is a diagnostic threshold for diabetes. Many adults with diabetes have an individualized target, often around 7%, adjusted for age, comorbidities and hypoglycemia risk. title: Hyperkalemia and RAAS drugs
text: Serum potassium above the laboratory upper limit (often about 5.0-5.5 mmol/L) is hyperkalemia. ACE inhibitors, ARBs and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists raise the risk, especially with reduced kidney function. Potassium and creatinine are usually checked soon after starting or changing these drugs. (Illustrative paraphrase for a demo, not clinical guidance; verify against the original guideline or label.)

title: Heart failure weight and BNP
text: Rapid weight gain (commonly cited as about 2 kg or more over a few days) can indicate fluid retention in heart failure. BNP and NT-proBNP rise with congestion and are also affected by age, kidney function and obesity. title: Levothyroxine monitoring and interactions
text: After starting or changing a levothyroxine dose, TSH is typically rechecked after about 6-8 weeks. Calcium and iron supplements reduce levothyroxine absorption; doses are commonly separated by about 4 hours. title: NSAIDs and kidney disease
text: NSAIDs can reduce kidney function and raise potassium, especially alongside ACE inhibitors or diuretics; avoidance is generally advised in CKD. (Illustrative paraphrase for a demo, not clinical guidance; verify against the original guideline or label.)
